positions.as_written: Repair aims to restore the anchor, so position matters as much as strength.
Compare a root tear against total meniscectomy rather than against partial resection.
Expect a medial posterior root tear to behave worse than a lateral one.
Use extrusion as the imaging sign that the mechanism has failed.
Treat root repair as a joint preservation operation rather than a symptom operation, because the mechanical case is about what happens next rather than about pain now.
Repair position relative to the native footprint centre.
Alignment correction, which sets the load the repair must carry.
Repair anatomically to the footprint centre, since direction of tension depends on it.
Assess and correct alignment alongside a root repair in a varus limb.
Measure residual extrusion postoperatively as the available proxy for restored function.
- The footprint centre must be restored to restore the direction of tension.
